author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence College field hockey extended its winning streak to four games Friday with a 4-1 victory over Sacred Heart at Yale in New Haven. Senior Bo Martina led the Friars with a career-high five points, scoring twice in the opening nine minutes and later assisting on the final goal.

Martina struck 1:57 into the game and again at 8:38, giving Providence early control. Lily Procaccianti added a goal at 17:01, and Martu Torre Festa completed the scoring at 42:22. Providence finished with a 16-6 advantage in total shots, a 7-4 edge in shots on goal and eight penalty corners to Sacred Heart’s three.

The result moved the Friars to 4-1 after an opening loss and raised Martina’s career total to 51 points, tied for 30th in program history. The balanced performance combined a fast start with sustained territorial pressure, limiting Sacred Heart’s opportunities while generating repeated set-piece chances. Providence continues its road stretch Sunday at noon against Hofstra, where it will try to carry the four-game run into another nonconference matchup.
dek: The Friars beat Sacred Heart 4-1 as senior Bo Martina produced a career-high five points with two goals and an assist.
headline: Providence field hockey wins fourth straight behind Bo Martina
